name: Publish/Subscribe Protocols
summary: Adversaries may communicate using publish/subscribe (pub/sub) application layer protocols to avoid detection/network filtering by blending in with existing traffic. Commands to the remote system, and often the results of those commands, will be embedded within the protocol traffic between the client and broker. strategies.name: Behavioral Detection of Publish/Subscribe Protocol Misuse for Command and Control

analytics.name: Analytic 2100
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies a Windows ICS asset initiating MQTT/AMQP/DDS communications to a broker/service not approved for the asset role, from a process not associated with authorized vendor or telemetry software. Require both a communication-matrix violation and destination/process/protocol corroboration; suppress approved brokers, telemetry collectors, vendor applications, and maintenance.

analytics.name: Analytic 2101
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies a Linux ICS service or process initiating MQTT/AMQP/DDS communications outside its approved broker/client relationship or from an unauthorized runtime/tool. Require communication-matrix violation plus process/destination/protocol corroboration; suppress approved telemetry, historian, gateway, vendor, and maintenance activity.

analytics.name: Analytic 2102
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies MQTT/AMQP/DDS sessions crossing an unexpected zone boundary, connecting an ICS client to an unapproved broker/service, or using client/topic/message behavior inconsistent with the documented pub/sub architecture. Require topology/identity/topic/destination violation; periodicity alone is not sufficient.

analytics.name: Analytic 2103
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies an embedded OT/IoT device establishing MQTT/AMQP/DDS communication with a broker/service outside its device-specific profile, using an unexpected client identity/topic, or crossing an unauthorized zone boundary. Fixed-function device behavior should be compared to the documented broker/topic/destination profile rather than a generic anomaly threshold.
